findings.message: Kanthal lists 2282 °F as the highest furnace temperature for coils in grooves; this kiln reaches 2345 °F. Kiln makers build cone 10 kilns this way, with shorter element life.
findings.reference: Kanthal key data for elements; electric-and-thermal.md §1.6 [S14]

findings.message: The tool chose 8 elements of 10 AWG wire (2.59 mm): the fewest elements that work, each with the thickest wire whose coil fits its groove. Kanthal recommends wire of 3 mm or more for the longest life in grooves. 12 elements would take 8 AWG (3.26 mm); set elements: 12 in the design's electric heat to use them.
findings.reference: electric-and-thermal.md §1.6 [S9, S13]

findings.message: The elements alone can't hold the top temperature; in this hybrid the burners take over before then.
Electrical work must follow your local code and be checked by a licensed electrician. These results are engineering guidance, not an approved design.
